original_question: Let H be a pr-graph, meaning a br-graph that is switching-equivalent to a graph with no pure blue edges. Let B_H := B x H be its bipartite resolution, where B is the purple K_2, so B_H has the parity-flip automorphism (i, v) -> (1 - i, v). A bipartite-min ordering of B_H is an ordering on each partite set that satisfies the underbar property, and it is special if every vertex has all neighbors joined by purple edges before its other neighbors. Is it true that B_H has a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it has a special bipartite-min ordering that is parity-symmetric, i.e. commutes with the parity flip?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Proposition 1.2: the bipartite-resolution reformulation for pr-graphs, expressing the existence of a special min ordering on H in terms of a parity-symmetric special bipartite-min ordering on its bipartite resolution B_H. Your draft is very close to the B_H-side of this proposition.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the paper's special setting of pr-graphs, the bipartite resolution B_H = B × H with the parity-flip involution (i,v) ↦ (1-i,v), and the key issue of whether a special bipartite-min ordering can be chosen to respect that involution. It also correctly uses the paper's 'special' condition that purple neighbours must come before the other neighbours.
missing_details: The paper's official introductory formulation is not just about B_H by itself: it links B_H back to H, namely to whether H has a special min ordering.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the question is for every pr-graph H in the paper's sense.

The standing graph-theoretic conventions should be stated explicitly: H is a br-graph/sign-patterned graph in which switching is allowed, and 'pr-graph' means that some switched representative has no pure blue edges.

The parity-symmetry condition should be written explicitly as compatibility of the two bipartite orders with the automorphism τ(i,v)=(1-i,v), rather than only informally as 'commutes with the parity flip.'
A special bipartite-min ordering is a pair of linear orders, one on each side of the bipartition; the draft alludes to this but does not fully spell out that both orders are part of the data.

If one wants the question to be fully paper-faithful, one should mention that this is a reduction statement in the introduction, adjacent to the main complexity conjecture and its reflexive-case theorem.
No ambient ring, field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifier is involved here; the missing data are graph-theoretic definitions and quantifiers, not algebraic side conditions.
refined_question: Let H be a finite pr-graph, i.e. a br-graph whose switching class contains a representative with no pure blue edges, and let B_H := B × H, where B is the purple K_2. Write τ(i,v) = (1-i,v) for the parity-flip automorphism of B_H. A special bipartite-min ordering of B_H is a pair of linear orders on the two bipartition classes satisfying the bipartite min underbar property and such that, for each vertex, all purple neighbours precede all non-purple neighbours. Is it true that B_H admits a special bipartite-min ordering if and only if it admits one that is τ-symmetric, meaning that the two part-orders are carried to each other by τ?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the paper's own reduction language: does a pr-graph H have a special min ordering exactly when its bipartite resolution B_H has a parity-symmetric special bipartite-min ordering?
justification: The draft clearly aims at the paper's bipartite-resolution reduction rather than at the broader complexity conjecture itself. The abstract says that the paper gives 'several tools for reducing the problem to the bipartite case', and among the numbered introductory statements the one nearest to your wording is Proposition 1.2. Conjecture 1.1 supplies the surrounding main classification problem, and Theorem 1.3 gives the nearby resolved case, but the draft's distinctive vocabulary—pr-graph, bipartite resolution B_H, parity flip, and special bipartite-min ordering—matches the reduction proposition. The main incompleteness is that the official formulation ties this symmetric-ordering question back to special min orderings of H itself, which your draft suppresses.
